clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-1191: battery.py and targeted.py on Polygon with every eth_call carrying a block number override of 98,688,601, one block after Salvador. On develop the instruction set is chosen by IsChicago, IsLisovoPro and IsLisovo (core/vm/evm.go:255-259) and no core/vm file read names Salvador.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/develop/core/vm/evm.go: the switch on chainRules.IsChicago, IsLisovoPro, IsLisovo, IsOsaka picks the table, and a case-insensitive search for Salvador in evm.go, jump_table.go, interpreter.go, instructions.go, mulmod_memo.go and contracts.go finds nothing. params/config.go uses Salvador only for IsSalvador and the BlockAlloc entry at 98688600, whose five targets (0xe4C4C39C..., 0x5392587814..., 0xc91ee057..., 0x3f701922..., 0x5227f603...) do not include the PoolManager 0x67366782805870060151383f4bbff9dab53e5cd6. out/battery-salvador.json records 99,985 ran, 0 mismatches, 0 errors on 137. The override does not show whether a build carries the MULMOD memo, as the item says. I read the memo independently: develop core/vm/mulmod_memo.go:55-66 keys on the full modulus and calls MulModWithReciprocal, and holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 uint256.go:688-715 is the same code as MulMod at :720-748 with the reciprocal supplied, so the result is a pure function of (x, y, m). core/parallel_state_processor.go:132 and :628 build a new EVM per task, so the memo is not shared between workers. FullMath.mulDiv reaches it at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24, :48 and :112.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Cycle 30 rerun of battery.py (99,985 vectors) and targeted.py (85,544 vectors) on the networks.json endpoints; MULMOD with modulus 2^256-1 and with a full-width denominator, as FullMath.mulDiv uses them, is among them.
clearedSpotChecks.note: out/battery.json shows 99,985 ran, 0 mismatches, 0 errors for each of 137, 56 and 43114, and out/targeted.json shows 85,544 with 0 mismatches. I ran my own read-only eth_call with a state-override contract that returns mulmod(a, b, n) on each networks.json endpoint for 10 cases (n = 2^256-1, 2^255+1, 2^255+7 and six random full-width moduli, including a = b = n = 2^256-1): all 30 answers equal (a*b) mod n. The line references src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24 and :48 are correct.
